name: Rengar
title: The Pridestalker

abilities.name: Unseen Predator
abilities.blurb: Innate:  Rengar generates Ferocity when he casts a basic ability or uses  Savagery's empowered attack, which expires after a period out of combat. At max Ferocity, his next basic ability consumes them to become empowered with an additional effect, gain an extra cast, and briefly grant him  bonus movement speed.

effects.description: Innate: Upon casting a basic ability or using Savagery's first attack, Rengar generates a stack of Ferocity for 1 second, stacking up 4 times but not refreshing on subsequent triggers (unexpected). At maximum stacks, his next basic ability consumes them all to become empowered with an additional effect and grant him an additional cast along with 30% / 40% / 50% (based on level) bonus movement speed for 1.5 seconds. Generated Ferocity is prevented from expiring for 10 seconds after dealing or taking damage, excluding damage dealt by damage over time or proc effects.
Innate: While in brush, Rengar gains Unseen Predator, which lingers for 0.35 seconds upon exiting brush. Unseen Predator is lost immediately if Rengar exits the brush using Flash or Hexflash.

Unseen Predator: Rengar's next basic attack on-attack generates 1 Ferocity if none of his current Ferocity was generated this way. The attack also has massively increased range and causes him to leap to the target's location if they are beyond his normal basic attack range, attacking the target upon arrival and landing 50 units in front of them.Rengar can cast any of his abilities during the dash. The start of the leap is the end of Rengar's attack windup, putting the attack timer on cooldown, triggering on-attack effects and additionally refreshing the Ferocity duration.

Innate - Bonetooth Necklace: Scoring a takedown against an enemy champion within 3 seconds of damaging them grants Rengar a Trophy, once per unique champion and up to 5. An additional Trophy is made available through the event The Hunt is On! with the Head of Kha'Zix. Trophies grant bonus attack damage equal to 1% - 36% (based on Trophies) bonus AD.

abilities.notes:
Rengar has a secondary resource bar that indicates how much Ferocity he currently has as pips.
Ferocity generated by Unseen Predator has a purple color.
Ferocity generated by his other abilities has a white color.
While out of combat, if abilities are used one after the other, only the first will count towards the 1 second Ferocity timer, without refreshing from the second cast. [5] (unexpected)
Reaching 4 Ferocity with an ability immediatelly grants access to empowered abilities, however reaching it with a brush attack will grant the access after a short delay - causing Rengar to still be able to cast normal abilities while at 4 Ferocity. [6] [7] (unexpected)
Only  Flash and  Hexflash instantly end Unseen Predator. Other  blink effects will still cause the buff to linger upon exiting the  brush area.
The attack deals  basic damage but is considered  ability damage for  Spear of Shojin.
While  grounded or  rooted, Rengar loses the enhanced  attack range from Unseen Predator.
 Rapid Firecannon's and  Savagery's bonus ranges are lost after 0.25 seconds upon gaining Unseen Predator, and are re-gained after 0.25 seconds upon losing Unseen Predator.
The same does not apply for other bonus ranges such as  Hexoptics C44's.
Rengar will only leap to a target if his basic attack timer has been refreshed (if not so he will not automatically attempt to path towards his target, despite them being within leap range).
The leap will consume  energized  on-attack but only expend it once the leap hits.
If the leap is  interrupted, the energized will be indefinitely stored in the background until expended by a successive leap. Only 1 energized may be stored, but another can continue to recharge on the buffbar.
While the energized is stored, normal basic attacks are prevented from expending any energized, however abilities may still expend the one from the buffbar. [8] (unexpected)
Rengar can freely use any  abilities, summoner spells, or item actives while leaping.
Using a  dash or  blink ability will interrupt the leap.
The attack from the leap will:
Not go off if the dash was interrupted.
Not go off if the target becomes  untargetable.
Go off at the end of the dash even if its normal destination is obstructed by boundaries he cannot cross (e.g. terrain,  The Hextech Ultimatum).
Go off regardless of distance the enemy travels away from Rengar's original location.
Go off even if Rengar loses  sight of the target.
Bonetooth Necklace uses different icons corresponding to the number of stacks acquired:
1 Stack: 
2 Stacks: 
3 Stacks: 
4 Stacks: 
5 Stacks: 
6th Stack:  Head of Kha'Zix

abilities.name: Savagery
abilities.blurb: Active:  Rengar gains  bonus attack speed for his next two  basic attacks. His next basic attack deals bonus physical damage and will  critically strike, dealing increased damage based on his  critical strike chance.

effects.description: Active: Rengar gains 40% bonus attack speed on his next two basic attacks on-attack within 3 seconds.

His first attack on-hit is empowered to stab the target, having an uncancellable windup, gaining 25 bonus range, and dealing additional physical damage. The attack can critically strike for (100% + 30%) AD bonus physical damage.

Ferocity Bonus: Savagery's damage is modified to deal 35 - 260 (based on level) (+ 20% AD) bonus physical damage. In addition to gaining another instance of the base attack speed on-cast, consuming the attack also grants 50% - 107% (based on level) bonus attack speed for 5 seconds.
Savagery resets Rengar's basic attack timer.

abilities.notes:
Casting Savagery does not  break stealth.
The bonus attack speed from the unempowered and empowered casts can stack with each other, if both are cast shortly one after another.
The empowered attack windup may still be manually cancelled when targeting jungle plants or  structures. [8] (unexpected)
Different attack speeds may desync the animation from the hit. [9] (unexpected)
 Interrupting  Unseen Predator's leap will shortly after replace Savagery's own animation with a normal basic attack animation. [10] (unexpected)
If  energized kills the target before the attack hits, Savagery won't be consumed but it will still grant free Ferocity. [11] (unexpected)
Savagery's empowered attack is consumed against jungle plants.
While the Ferocity timer is not running, if the attack  misses or is  dodged it will grant a permanent Ferocity stack until the timer is triggered and refreshed. [12] (unexpected)
The additional damage is tagged as  proc damage,  basic damage, and  spell damage, and applies other  on-hit effects as well as  life steal as normal.
It is also part of a separate cast instance - potentially allowing an extra stack of  Eclipse and  Electrocute (e.g while using  Black Cleaver). [13] (unexpected)
The in-game extended tooltip incorrectly states that the additional damage is reduced against structures. [14] (unexpected)

abilities.name: Battle Roar
abilities.blurb: Passive:  Rengar stores grey health equal to a portion of damage taken within a brief moment.

effects.description: Passive: Rengar stores 50% of the post-mitigation damage he has taken in the last 1.5 seconds as grey health on his health bar, increased to 100% of damage taken from monsters.
Active: Rengar roars, dealing magic damage to nearby enemies and 65 - 137.65 (based on level) bonus magic damage to monsters, and consuming his grey health to heal for the same amount.
Ferocity Bonus: Battle Roar's damage is modified to deal 50 - 240 (based on level) (+ 80% AP) magic damage. Rengar cleanses himself from all crowd control.

abilities.notes:
Grey health will not be consumed upon casting Battle Roar despite visually appearing so. It will only ever expire after its duration ends.
The ability will visibly attempt to but fail to buffer if cast during a non-ability cast time. [2] (unexpected)

abilities.name: Bola Strike
abilities.blurb: Active:  Rengar throws a bola in the target direction that deals  physical damage and briefly  slows the first enemy hit,  revealing them for a short time.

effects.description: Active: Rengar throws a bola in the target direction that deals physical damage to the first enemy hit and slows them for 1.75 seconds, as well as revealing them for 2 seconds and granting sight of a 150-unit radius around them for the same duration.
Ferocity Bonus: Bola Strike's damage is modified to deal 50 - 335 (based on level) (+ 80% bonus AD) physical damage. The target is rooted instead of slowed.

abilities.notes:
If Rengar casts  Savagery and/or  Battle Roar during Bola Strike's cast time, he will buffer them and cast them when Bola Strike completes.
This ability will cast from wherever the caster is at the end of the cast time.
Bola Strike maintains its casting angle direction in relation to Rengar if he moves during the cast time.

abilities.name: Thrill of the Hunt
abilities.blurb: Passive:  Rengar also gains  Unseen Predator while  camouflaged.

effects.description: Passive: Rengar also gains Unseen Predator while camouflaged from any source.

Active: Rengar prowls for a duration, gaining bonus movement speed. After a 2-second delay, he also becomes camouflaged and gains Unseen Predator.

The camouflage can only last up to 14 seconds. (unexpected)
During this time, Rengar will detect the nearest enemy champion in range, revealing and gaining sight of a 100-unit radius around them. Enemies detected are revealed for the remaining full duration.
The nearest detected enemy within 1600 range is also marked, alerting all of their allies within 1200 range about Rengar's presence.

Rengar's next basic attack within 125 range against any enemy or with Unseen Predator to the marked enemy deals 100% AD additional physical damage, then inflicts armor reduction for 4 seconds.
The target is revealed until the leap has finished.
Attacking or casting abilities other than Savagery ends Thrill of the Hunt immediately.

abilities.notes:
Thrill of the Hunt's duration starts on-cast.
It is not expected for the camouflage duration to be lower than the total effect duration. [10] (unexpected)
If a  revealed enemy  stealths, their  true sight debuff will be removed, dropping aggro. [11] [12] (unexpected)
The debuff will be reapplied after 0.033s if they get back in range.
Using a basic attack  breaks the stealth at the start of the attack windup.
Unlike other champions that break the stealth at the start of attack windup, Rengar may automatically start attacking a nearby target if the player's "Auto Attack" setting is turned on. [13] (unexpected)
The ability applies a mark on the target at the start of attack windup that is successively consumed when the basic attack hits to apply the effect.
If the attack is prevented or blocked (e.g. by  knocking down Rengar when  leaping) then the effect will not be applied.
The mark will however still linger for a very short period after that, allowing Rengar to consume it with a quick basic attack. [14]
The ability deals  basic damage.
Unlike other ability empowered attacks (i.e  Kled's  Violent Tendencies,  Malphite's  Thunderclap), the additional damage is also tagged as  proc damage - preventing triggering certain effects (e.g  Malignance). [15] (unexpected)
It is also part of a separate cast instance - potentially allowing an extra stack of  Eclipse and  Electrocute (e.g while using  Black Cleaver). [16] (unexpected)
The Unseen Predator buff may randomly end before a melee attack hits, causing the ability's effects to go through but without generating Ferocity. [17] (unexpected)
Rengar may sometimes be able to still leap away after consuming the ability with a melee basic attack. [18] (unexpected)
Rengar discerns a distinct  heart beat instead of the usual  true sight indicator. This indicator will be removed when out of range, but the target will remain revealed.
Thrill of the Hunt has an indicator that appears above the target(s) when Rengar is nearby. Some skins have a unique indicator.

lore: Rengar is a ferocious vastayan trophy hunter who lives for the thrill of tracking down and killing dangerous creatures. He scours the world for the most fearsome beasts he can find, especially seeking any trace of Kha'Zix, the void creature who scratched out his eye. Rengar stalks his prey neither for food nor glory, but for the sheer beauty of the pursuit.
